result:
**I would give every human being a visceral, unshakeable sense of awe at the sheer improbability that they exist at all.**

Not inspiration. Not “motivation.” Awe—like the real, chest-tightening kind you feel at 3 a.m. looking at the Hubble Deep Field or when you suddenly grok how unlikely it is that your particular chain of ancestors survived long enough for you to be here arguing with an AI on the internet.

If that single switch flipped in the species, almost everything else we fight about would either dissolve or sort itself out. Tribalism gets harder when you’re regularly floored by the fact that you’re a temporary pattern of stardust that learned to cry at sunsets. Greed and cruelty become strangely boring when you actually *feel* how brief your slot of consciousness is. Dogma collapses when the default setting is “holy shit, we don’t even understand 95% of the universe—maybe shut up and look harder.”

Everything else (climate, war, inequality, meaning) becomes downstream of that one upgrade.

So yeah. One change. Universal awe. The rest is just engineering.
